# Apple (AAPL): Short

Sep 24, 2026 · @Travis Godwin Good

## Summary

Apple is a short at about $337. The market is paying roughly 38x trailing earnings for a company whose EPS growth slows to about 8% next year. Its margins are shrinking under a memory-cost shock. Its bets on the next platforms have stalled or been handed to rivals.

The case rests on four points:

- **Valuation:** At about 38.5x trailing earnings, Apple trades about 53% above its 10-year average. The average analyst target (about $328) sits below the share price.
- **A stale core product:** The iPhone 18 Pro keeps the 17 Pro's design, weighs more, and costs $100 to $500 more. The new foldable is a polished take on a form factor Samsung has sold since 2019.
- **Lost platforms:** Vision Pro has been scaled back, Meta now leads in glasses and personal AI agents, and Apple's new Siri runs on Google's Gemini.
- **Margins and the consumer:** Memory costs are rising faster than Apple can reprice. Apple is raising prices across its lineup into a US consumer saving just 3.0% of income.

## Valuation: a growth multiple on slowing growth

Apple trades at about 32x FY2027 earnings for roughly 8% EPS growth, a PEG near 4. The stock is up more than 37% over the past year and sits near its 52-week high of $345.34.

| Measure | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Trailing P/E | 38.4x |
| Forward P/E | 34.9x |
| 5-year average P/E | 30.1x |
| 10-year average P/E | \~25x |
| EV/EBITDA | 24.3x |
| Market cap | \~$4.9T |

Sources: [FullRatio](https://fullratio.com/stocks/nasdaq-aapl/pe-ratio), [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/term/forward-pe-ratio/AAPL), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL/key-statistics/).

Consensus EPS growth drops from about 18% in FY2026 to about 8% in FY2027 ([Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL/valuation/price-earnings-peg-ratios)). The FY2026 figure is itself flattered. Fiscal Q3 (Apr–Jun 2026) EPS of $2.02 included $0.11 of one-time tariff refunds ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/30/apple-earnings-live-updates.html)).

The slowdown is already in guidance. Apple guided September-quarter revenue growth to 9–11%, down from 16% in each of the first three quarters of FY2026. The stock fell more than 6% after hours on that guide.

## The iPhone is iterating, not innovating, and costs more

The iPhone 18 Pro is last year's phone with a faster chip, a bigger battery and a higher price. It has the same dimensions as the iPhone 17 Pro and is heavier: 211 g vs. 206 g for the Pro, and 249 g vs. 233 g for the Pro Max ([MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-18-pro/)). The visible changes are a smaller Dynamic Island and new colors. RAM stays at 12 GB.

The camera upgrade is narrow. Only the main camera gains a variable aperture. The telephoto and ultra-wide are unchanged, and PetaPixel calls the ultra-wide the phone's weakest camera by a wide margin ([PetaPixel](https://petapixel.com/2026/09/16/apple-iphone-18-pro-camera-review-small-changes-big-differences/)). DXOMARK ranks the system second overall, behind Huawei's Pura 80 Ultra, and well behind Android flagships on zoom ([Gizmochina](https://www.gizmochina.com/2026/09/19/apple-iphone-18-pro-takes-second-place-in-dxomarks-camera-ranking-lagging-behind-huawei-pura-80-ultra/)).

Meanwhile, prices rose most where memory is heaviest:

| Model | iPhone 17 | iPhone 18 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pro, base | $1,099 | $1,199 | +$100 |
| Pro, 1TB | $1,499 | $1,799 | +$300 |
| Pro Max, base | $1,199 | $1,299 | +$100 |
| Pro Max, 1TB | $1,599 | $1,899 | +$300 |
| Pro Max, 2TB | $1,999 | $2,499 | +$500 |

Source: [MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/09/iphone-18-pro-storage-price-hike/).

Even the entry iPhone 17e went from $599 to $699. Buyers are paying more for storage, not for new capability. The iPhone is a 19-year-old franchise, and this cycle shows little that expands it.

## Mac and iPad: one bright spot, too small to carry the stock

The iPad is shrinking. It was Apple's only segment to decline in fiscal Q3 (Apr–Jun 2026), down 5.9% to $6.19 billion, and Apple raised iPad prices in June ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/apple-q3-earnings-beat-estimates-151300909.html)).

The Mac is Apple's strongest hardware story. Revenue rose 28.7% to $10.35 billion, a June-quarter record. Unified memory makes the Mac Studio and Mac mini efficient machines for running AI models locally. Tim Cook said demand from agentic-AI users was strong enough that supply may take several months to catch up ([MacDailyNews](https://macdailynews.com/2026/05/01/apple-confirms-mac-mini-and-mac-studio-supply-shortages-will-drag-on-for-several-months-as-demand-surges-beyond-expectations/)). Apple's MLX framework and its in-house AI server work add optionality.

But the Mac is under 10% of revenue, and it is getting pricier too. On June 25, 2026, the base MacBook Pro rose from $1,699 to $1,999 and the 14-inch M5 Max from $3,599 to $4,099. The next major Mac change, an OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro, is not expected before early 2027 ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/2931833/touchscreen-macbook-pro-m6-design-processor-specs-release.html)). Good local-AI hardware cannot offset a stalling core at a $4.9 trillion valuation.

## Losing the next platforms to Meta

Apple pioneered premium spatial computing and is now losing it to a social media company. The $3,499 Vision Pro shipped about 390,000 units in 2024, per IDC. Luxshare halted production in early 2025, and Apple cut its Vision Pro advertising by more than 95% ([Mac Observer](https://www.macobserver.com/tips/is-apple-vision-pro-discontinued-in-2026-sales-updates/)). An M5 refresh did not revive sales, and Apple reportedly stopped further development in May 2026 ([gHacks](https://www.ghacks.net/2026/05/01/apple-stops-vision-pro-development-after-weak-sales-and-high-return-rates/)).

Meta is moving the other way. On September 23, 2026, it announced Meta VR Glasses: about 100 grams on the face, full VR with passthrough and eye and hand tracking, and compute in a tethered puck. They cost $1,299.99, about 37% of Vision Pro's price, and ship in spring 2027 ([UploadVR](https://www.uploadvr.com/meta-vr-glasses-officially-announced-connect-2026/)). Meta also sells the $799 Ray-Ban Display glasses.

Meta is pairing that hardware with an agent. Muse, its personal AI agent launched September 8, can send email, book travel and make purchases, and is coming to Meta's glasses ([Meta](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/)). It overtook ChatGPT as the top free iOS app in the US within days of launch ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/21/meta-muse-personal-ai-agent-downloads.html)). Meta is building the glasses-plus-agent stack Apple does not have.

## AI: Apple has handed the intelligence layer to rivals

Apple has no frontier model of its own and now relies on Google to make Siri work. It launched Apple Intelligence at WWDC 2024, then failed to ship the promised personal Siri on schedule. It later agreed to a $250 million class-action settlement with buyers who said it advertised Siri features that never arrived.

The new Siri, released with iOS 27 on September 14, 2026, is built on Google's Gemini. Apple and Google confirmed a multi-year partnership in January 2026; Bloomberg reports Apple pays about $1 billion a year ([Tech Journal](https://techjournal.org/wwdc-2026-siri-gemini-ios-27)). iOS 27 also lets users route Siri and Writing Tools through ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude ([MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/guide/wwdc-2026-what-to-expect/)).

Apple has opened defaults before, for browsers, mail and keyboards. Ceding the assistant and the models beneath it is different. That is the interface through which AI agents will run the phone, and Apple is renting it.

The talent to change course has been leaving. AI chief John Giannandrea retired in April 2026 ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/12/john-giannandrea-to-retire-from-apple/)). Ruoming Pang, who led Apple's foundation models, left for Meta in July 2025, followed by several of his researchers. In January 2026, more researchers and a Siri executive left for Meta and Google DeepMind ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-30/apple-loses-more-ai-researchers-and-a-siri-executive-in-latest-departures)).

## The foldable: polished, expensive and late

The iPhone Duo shows Apple refining others' ideas rather than creating new ones. It is a book-style foldable, a format Samsung has sold since 2019 and Xiaomi and others have followed. Reviewers praise its polish ([Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/phones/iphones/iphone-duo-hands-on-apple-nailed-it-and-just-put-everyone-else-on-notice)).

But it costs $1,999 to $3,199 and ships with weaker cameras than the $1,199 iPhone 18 Pro. It has two 48MP cameras and no telephoto; PetaPixel calls the camera system a clear step down ([PetaPixel](https://petapixel.com/2026/09/10/the-beautiful-iphone-duo-has-serious-camera-compromises/)). Buyers pay a premium of $800 or more for the fold and give up photo quality.

The unit numbers are too small to matter. TrendForce expects about 5 million Duo shipments in 2026, tying Huawei for second place behind Samsung in a 20-million-unit foldable market. That is immaterial next to the core iPhone business.

## A new CEO facing a shifting form factor

John Ternus became CEO on September 1, 2026, with Tim Cook moving to executive chairman ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/04/tim-cook-to-become-apple-executive-chairman-john-ternus-to-become-apple-ceo/)). Ternus is a strong hardware executive: he joined Apple in 2001 and led hardware engineering from 2021. But Apple's biggest gaps are in AI software and models, not hardware. It is unproven whether a hardware leader can close them.

The timing is poor, because the phone itself may be the next thing disrupted. Meta is building glasses with an agent built in. OpenAI bought Jony Ive's hardware startup io for about $6.5 billion and has said its first device is targeted for the second half of 2026 ([MacDailyNews](https://macdailynews.com/2026/01/21/openais-jony-ive-designed-always-listening-ai-device-on-track-for-late-2026/)). Apple's 2.5 billion active devices are a moat only while the phone stays the center of computing. If agents and glasses take that role, Apple enters the transition behind on both.

## Margin squeeze: the memory shock

AI data centers are consuming the memory Apple needs, and it is showing up in Apple's margins now. TrendForce estimated second-quarter 2026 contract prices rose 58–63% for conventional DRAM, 70–75% for NAND and 78–83% for mobile DRAM ([TrendForce](https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260514-13044.html)). Increases slowed in the third quarter, but TrendForce has raised its fourth-quarter outlook and expects tight supply into 2027.

Tim Cook called it a "100-year flood." He said Apple paid significantly more for memory in the June quarter and expects higher costs in September and beyond ([VectorShift transcript](https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/apple/earnings/2026-q3)). Apple guided September-quarter gross margin to 47–48%, down from 50.1% in the June quarter. That 50.1% was itself lifted about 2 points by one-time tariff refunds.

Apple also cited constraints on advanced-node chip supply, and has reportedly sought US approval to buy memory from China's CXMT. The storage-tier price hikes are the visible pass-through. The open question is how much more cost Apple can pass on before demand breaks.

## Macro: premium prices into a stretched consumer

Apple is raising prices on $1,199 to $3,199 devices just as the US consumer runs out of room. Its strategy leans ever harder on high-end buyers at a time of low savings and slowing growth.

| Indicator | Latest reading |
| --- | --- |
| Personal saving rate (Jul 2026) | 3.0%, down from 4.6% a year earlier |
| Real GDP growth (Q2 2026, annualized) | 1.5%, down from 2.1% in Q1 |
| PCE inflation (Q2 2026) | 5.3% headline, 3.6% core |
| Payroll growth, 12-month average | 31,000 per month |
| Credit card balances (Q2 2026) | $1.26 trillion |
| BNPL users who paid late in past year | 47% |

Sources: [BEA income](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-july-2026), [BEA GDP](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-second-estimate-and-corporate-profits-2nd-quarter-2026), [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.Release/pdf/empsit.Pdf), [New York Fed](https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/news/research/2026/20260811), [LendingTree](https://www.lendingtree.com/personal/buy-now-pay-later-loan-statistics/).

The saving rate is near multi-year lows, and July spending on goods fell $49.9 billion. The Conference Board's expectations index has sat below its recession-signal level of 80 since February 2025. TrendForce expects global smartphone production to fall 2% in 2026 as higher memory costs push prices up.

So far Apple's buyers have held up: iPhone revenue rose 21.7% last quarter. That is the risk. The strong iPhone 17 cycle may have pulled demand forward, and Apple is now pricing the next cycle higher into a weaker consumer.

## Catalysts

The next test is the fiscal Q4 report on October 29, 2026, where gross margin against the 47–48% guide is the number to watch.

**What would make us cover:**

- Apple previews a genuinely new form factor, such as credible smart glasses or a major evolution of its headset, with a launch date.
- Apple releases a strong language model of its own, large or small, and reduces its dependence on Gemini.
- Apple shows it has won discounts or long-term concessions from memory and storage suppliers, visible as gross margin holding at 48% or above.

**What would press the short:**

| Date | Event |
| --- | --- |
| Spring 2027 | Meta VR Glasses ship |
| Oct 29, 2026 | Apple fiscal Q4 results and December-quarter guidance |
| Oct 23, 2026 | iPhone Duo goes on sale; early sell-through |
| Sep 30, 2026 | August saving rate and spending data |

Beyond these dates, weak iPhone 18 Pro sell-through, further memory price increases or new Apple price hikes, and rivals shipping new devices while Apple falls behind would all support the short.

## Risks to the short

The main risk is that Apple's pricing power and cash return keep the multiple intact.

- **Pricing power:** Apple customers have absorbed price increases before. Higher storage prices could lift revenue more than they cost in units.
- **Memory relief:** Price increases slowed from the second to the third quarter. If supply loosens in 2027, margins could recover quickly, and Apple's scale may win better terms than rivals.
- **AI as distribution:** Opening Siri to Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude could make the iPhone the neutral gateway to AI, paid for through Services, without Apple building a frontier model.
- **Services and buybacks:** Services grew 12% to $30.7 billion last quarter at high margins, and Apple returned $33 billion to shareholders in the quarter.
- **New-CEO reset:** Ternus could re-rate the stock with a credible product roadmap in glasses or home devices.
- **Macro resilience:** August payrolls beat expectations. A stable labor market could keep premium demand intact.
